title: Transient boost lanes: operator-configurable surge throttling and invoice attribution
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Summary: Implement a transient boost lanes feature that allows operators to grant short-lived, tenant-scoped surge capacity (ad-hoc boosts) with clear attribution for overage billing. Goals: 1) an operator-controlled 'boost lane' that can be attached to a tenant for N minutes/hours, 2) ensure throughput guarantees are honored for reserved capacity while allowing regulated burst capacity, 3) produce deterministic per-tenant metering that separates base committed usage from temporary boost usage for accurate invoicing, 4) provide console controls, alerts, and audit trails for boosts, 5) fail-safe automatic expiry and graceful throttling fallback when boost ends or capacity is constrained.

Technical approach: 1) Coordinator: add a transient-boost token in the routing layer that routes eligible requests to surge pools with soft quotas and token-level attribution metadata. 2) Surge pools: implement ephemeral pool abstraction backed by pre-warmed instances that can be drained or reclaimed; use existing headroom allocator code paths but with separate accounting and quicker preemption policy. 3) Billing: extend metering pipeline to emit three categories per request: committed, boost, and overflow. Boost usage carries a different rate and optional per-boost cap. 4) Operator controls: API and Console UI to create boosts (tenant, duration, max tps, optional cost-limit), revoke early, and view audit log. 5) Autoscaling interaction: boosts can pin extra capacity but must respect global autoscaler safety limits; implement congestion signals to limit boost admission when fleet-wide headroom < threshold. 6) Observability: new metrics (boost_allocated_tps, boost_consumed_tokens, boost_expiry_events), tracing tags for boost_id, and billing reconciliation dashboards.

Acceptance criteria: - Boosts can be created via API/Console with a duration, max TPS, and cost cap. - Requests routed during boost are labeled and metered as 'boost' in billing pipeline. - Boosts auto-expire and system reverts to committed or fallback models without request loss. - Operator can revoke boosts and view audit logs. - Sufficient load tests demonstrate no regressing to SLOs for committed tenants. - End-to-end e2e test and a billing reconciliation job to validate invoices against raw events.

Related docs: Confluence design doc: https://redwood-internal.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENG/pages/TRANSIENT+BOOST+LANES, design spec draft in Google Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/boost-lanes-draft
comments: 2025-02-14 - Ava Chen: Created ticket after spike investigating short-lived surge use cases from Customer X. Spike notes: latency impact is acceptable if we isolate KV caches per pool. Linked design doc.

2025-02-19 - Diego Morales: Implemented prototype of routing token and added unit tests for boost labeling. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/3842. Observability stubbed into metrics collector.
2025-02-25 - Priya Nair (PM): Reviewed scope; requested cost-limit per-boost and console UX for one-click revoke. Added requirement to surface predicted cost before activation.
2025-03-01 - SRE rotation (Luca Rossi): Runbook drafted for boost misuse (operator error) and auto-expiry verification steps. Added alerts for boost_creation_rate > 5/hour.

2025-03-05 - Diego Morales: Integration tests failing intermittently under heavy autoscale churn; suspected race between pre-warm reclaim and boost admission. Plan: add pre-emption grace window and stronger locking around node assignments.
